name: Reflexion
institution: Northeastern University, Princeton University, MIT (authors: Noah Shinn, Federico Cassano, Edward Berman, Ashwin Gopinath, Karthik Narasimhan, Shunyu Yao)
what_evolved: Context记忆与提示 (no model weight updates). The agent policy is parameterized by a long-term episodic memory of self-reflections paired with fixed LLM parameters, rather than updated weights.
skill_as_artifact: Yes. Self-reflective verbal feedback is stored as standalone textual artifacts in an episodic memory buffer ('mem'), persisted across trials and reused as context. Form: natural-language reflection summaries.
skill_encoding: 自然语言 (free-form natural-language self-reflection text generated by an LLM). No code/graph/embedding form in the core method (vector/SQL DBs suggested as future work).
skill_granularity: 见解 (insight). Each artifact is a verbal experience/lesson distilled from a full failed trajectory (e.g. 'I should have checked the drawer first'), serving as actionable self-hints.
how_method: reward-based via verbal/textual feedback acting as a 'semantic gradient' signal; non-gradient policy optimization in text space (verbal RL). An Actor-Evaluator-Self-Reflection loop amplifies a sparse scalar/binary reward into natural-language feedback appended to memory to steer the next trial. No gradient/SFT/RL weight updates.
learning_signal_source: Hybrid: environmental reward (compiler/test execution, exact-match grading, binary task-success), self-written unit tests (programming), LLM-as-judge / hand-written heuristics (decision-making), and self-reflection (LLM-generated verbal critique of its own trajectory).
reward_granularity: outcome (a single scalar/binary reward per trajectory/trial; e.g. pass/fail, exact-match, task-complete).
learning_paradigm: online; on-policy (the agent learns from its own freshly generated trajectories; no off-policy replay of external data).
when_evolve: intra-test-time (iterative online learning across repeated trials of the same task within a single solve; memory is reset between distinct tasks in the main experiments).
trigger: 失败触发 (failure-triggered). Loop re-runs Actor->Evaluator->Self-Reflection until the Evaluator passes or a max-trial budget is reached.
library_structure: 扁平 (flat sliding-window memory). The last Omega (typically 1-3) reflection entries are kept and prepended to context; entries beyond the window are dropped. Paper notes vector-DB/SQL as future extensions.
retrieval_method: Direct reuse of the sliding window: all retained reflections are concatenated into the actor prompt. No semantic/vector retrieval (collection is tiny), no workflow matching.
validation: Execution-based validation (compiler + self-generated unit tests for coding; environment task-success for AlfWorld; exact-match grading for HotpotQA), supplemented by LLM-judge / hand-written heuristics to detect failure/non-progress (e.g. repeated-action cycles, >30 actions).
error_correction: 自我修订 (self-revision): on failure the agent regenerates a new attempt conditioned on its reflected lessons; for code it can also recognize incorrect self-tests and keep the prior implementation intact to avoid harmful edits.
test_env: Diverse: AlfWorld (text-world sequential decision-making), HotpotQA (multi-hop QA reasoning), HumanEval/MBPP/LeetcodeHardGym (Python & Rust code generation). LeetcodeHardGym is a new 40-question hard benchmark introduced by the paper.
backbone_model: Model-agnostic LLM framework; experiments use GPT-3 (AlfWorld via ReAct few-shot), GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 (coding / reasoning). Chain-of-Thought and ReAct used as Actor modules.
where_deploy: general (general-purpose across sequential decision-making, language reasoning, and programming).
metrics: success_rate (AlfWorld tasks solved), pass@1 (HumanEval/MBPP/LeetcodeHard), exact-match accuracy (HotpotQA); also test-quality confusion metrics (TP/FN/FP/TN of self-generated unit tests).
key_results: No weight updates / no fine-tuning. HumanEval pass@1 = 91% (beating GPT-4's 80% SOTA at the time). AlfWorld: 130/134 tasks solved, +22% absolute over ReAct baseline within 12 trials. HotpotQA: +20% improvement (CoT(GT)+Reflexion +14% over CoT(GT)). MBPP Rust 75.4%, HumanEval Rust 68%. Ablations show both test-generation and self-reflection are necessary (self-reflection alone regresses to 52% on HumanEval-Rust-50).
limitations: scalability (memory hard-capped at 1-3 entries by context length; no persistent cross-task library); controllability (no formal success guarantee, may converge to non-optimal local minima); eval-hacking (flaky/self-written tests yield false positives, e.g. MBPP-Python regresses below GPT-4 baseline due to 16.3% false-positive test rate); transferability (reflections are task-specific, memory resets per task); strong dependence on the LLM's self-evaluation ability; reliance on isolated sandbox for autonomous code execution.
